Name: Adobe Acrobat Reader
Description: The Reader bootstrapper wrapped and silenced - with a plain warning that the supported enterprise route is a different one.
Awkwardness: Reader is not really an EXE at all. The download is a bootstrapper around AcroRead.msi, and Adobe's supported enterprise route is to extract it, build a transform with the Customization Wizard and deploy MSI plus MST together. That route cannot go through this tool: Windows Installer will not nest one MSI inside another, so if you need a transform you should deploy the extracted MSI directly in Intune and stop here. The second problem outlives the packaging: Reader patches itself. Adobe's monthly .msp updates move the ProductVersion under you within days of deployment, so any detection rule pinned to the version you shipped drifts out of true on its own, and the package in Intune stops describing what is actually on the estate.
DownloadNotes: Take the enterprise download, not the consumer web installer - the consumer one is a downloader stub with no payload of its own. If you need a transform, extract the MSI instead: AcroRdrDC*.exe -sfx_o"C:\reader" -sfx_ne, then deploy AcroRead.msi with TRANSFORMS= directly.
Notes: NOT tested in this repository. The switches are transcribed from Adobe's enterprise deployment documentation and have not been run here.

If your deployment needs a customisation transform, do not use this blueprint. Extract the MSI, pair it with your MST, and deploy that MSI in Intune - a Windows Installer package cannot be repackaged inside another one, and 'msimaker analyze' will say the same if you point it at AcroRead.msi.

Adobe documents /sAll for a fully silent install, /rs to suppress the reboot, and /msi to pass properties through to the inner MSI; EULA_ACCEPT=YES is one of those properties. Confirm all four against the documentation for the build you downloaded.
No uninstall action is wired up. Reader registers its own MSI entry in Programs and Features; take its ProductCode from a test device and remove it with msiexec /x rather than guessing a path.
Reader self-updates. Whatever version you ship here will not be the version on the device a month later - do not build a detection rule that assumes otherwise.
Set Version to the Reader build you downloaded.

Arp.Comments: Adobe Acrobat Reader's enterprise bootstrapper wrapped as an MSI. Switches from vendor documentation, untested.
